title: Add KMS residency lock and audit-throttle middleware
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Several customers in regulated jurisdictions requested stronger enforcement that KMS keys used for encryption are resident in the tenant-declared region and that noisy audit streams do not overwhelm the central audit pipeline. This PR introduces two coordinated middleware components: (1) an operator-scoped KMS residency lock that enforces per-operator KMS region affinity and rejects (or transparently routes) requests that would use a cross-region CMK unless explicit consent is present; (2) an audit-throttle middleware that deduplicates high-volume audit events and applies configurable rate limits and burst controls to audit-forwarding so the audit ingestion system remains available under noisy tenants.

Summary of changes: added new middleware in the KMS and audit stacks, updated RBAC v2 policy checks to include a temporal operator claim used during short-lived cross-region escalation, added a small migration to backfill residency tags for recent audit entries, and a feature-flagged canary rollout with observability and rollback hooks. This is primarily server-side code with a small config/ops surface in deploy/feature-flags and docs for enterprise customers.

Design notes: - KMS residency lock operates at the operator service boundary: it inspects the request's operator identity (claim) and tenant residency metadata. If the key candidate is outside the tenant region, middleware will consult the ConsentStore; absent consent, the request is rejected with a 403 and a structured audit event that includes the reason. - Audit-throttle is placed before the audit-forwarder. It implements keyed sampling + token-bucket per-tenant controls, and a dedupe window for identical audit payloads. Dedup and throttle rules are configurable per-tenant via the console and default to conservative limits. - RBAC change: introduce a short-lived claim type "operator:region-escalation" for automated canaries and on-call operator flows; checks are additive and behind a feature flag. We explicitly avoid widening existing permissions by requiring the claim and audit evidence.

Checklist: - [x] Middleware implementation and unit tests - [x] Integration tests (KMS residency rejection + consent flow) - [x] Migration script to backfill "residency_region" audit tags - [x] Feature flag + console documentation - [x] Metrics and dashboards (latency, throttle_rejected, dedupe_rate) - [x] Canaries and rollout plan in deploy/feature-flags.yaml

Commits: - feat(kms): operator-scoped residency lock middleware
- feat(audit): audit-throttle middleware with dedupe window
- perf(middleware): batch consent cache lookups and add circuit-breaker
- test: integration tests for residency and audit throttle flows
- ops: add feature flag and rollout config, migration backfill script

High level files changed: ["service/kms/middleware_residency.go", "service/audit/middleware_throttle.go", "pkg/rbac/v2/claims.go", "tools/migrations/backfill_residency_tags.sql", "deploy/feature-flags.yaml", "docs/enterprise/kms-residency.md", "tests/integration/test_kms_residency.py", "tests/integration/test_audit_throttle.py", "service/audit/audit_forwarder.go", "pkg/consent/consentstore.go", "pkg/metrics/metrics_definitions.yaml", "Makefile"]

Review conversation (high level): - Alex: requested clearer metric names and suggested moving dedupe default from 60s -> 30s to reduce perceived duplication during spikes. Implementation updated and metric names prefixed with "residency_" and "audit_throttle_". - Priya: asked for explicit consent-store TTL and circuit-breaker instrumentation. Added tests for consent cache eviction and a Prometheus gauge for circuit-breaker state. - Rory: asked for a migration rollback plan; added documentation and an idempotent SQL script that can be re-run safely. Minor lint fixes and added a unit test to cover a previously flaky path.

CI summary: Initial CI run failed on a flaky integration test (tests/integration/test_audit_throttle.py::test_dedupe_window) in the concurrency harness. Reran CI with the stabilized harness and tests passed. Full checks: unit, integration (canaries), linters, schema checks. All gates green on rerun.

Operational notes: Rollout is gated behind feature flag "redwood.kms_residency_lock". Canary at 10% for 48h measuring reject_rate, latency_p95, audit_throttle_rejects. If reject_rate > 0.5% for non-test tenants or latency_p95 increases > 20% we will rollback. Migration backfill is safe to run offline and is idempotent; ops runbook included in docs/enterprise/kms-residency.md.

Related work: ENG-7432 (residency policy audit), SEC-211 (enterprise KMS compliance checklist). This complements previous residency-oriented changes but differs by focusing on operator-scoped enforcement plus audit ingestion protection.

Merge: Squash and merge after approvals. Changelog entry and release note added.

release_notes: Adds operator-scoped KMS residency enforcement and an audit-throttle middleware to protect audit ingestion. Feature-flagged; canary rollout planned. Includes migration to backfill residency tags and observability updates.

customer_impact: Customers without cross-region consent will see 403 on attempted cross-region CMK usage when the flag is enabled; documentation provided for requesting consent or using region-compatible keys. Audit ingestion stability improved for noisy tenants.
